verdict.why: X gives the implementer the stronger acceptance tests for the two claims that matter: the defect appeared only in the tested configuration, and a reused screenshot came from the build under review. R8–R10 require a failed checklist item, a reference capture and differing axes; R14 checks the stand capture's build, cell, scenario, step and hash. Y's C4 usefully requires a persona control from the same round, but permits a config-only claim on an axis that was never applied. C7/T-19 explicitly lets stand evidence pass without a build comparison. Both preserve the scenario × persona matrix and leave agent-tester unchanged. Operationally, X's separately dated rows make December 7 deliverable without the stand and give the December 21 dependency a clear blocked state (D19, Rollout). Y is leaner and better specifies self-capture fallback, but its gate can certify evidence that its own intake procedure says not to use.
risks: X R3–R4 impose panel composition quotas and discontinuous viewport bands not requested by the brief. A 380-wide phone fails every class, creating avoidable capture and panel rework.
X R8 checks contradiction by checklist item rather than defect and does not require the same round. A different text-fit defect, or a stale control, can invalidate a legitimate finding.

Neither option establishes that the stand exports the required metadata or that the sender has a key. Y Q5–Q6 correctly identify both as dependencies; December 21 is conditional, not a confirmed integration date.
Both allow entirely unconfigured legacy panels. Compatibility avoids a release-day break, but shipping the gate does not itself put configurations on every project's ten portraits.
